ei.title: Shills Worked Better for Using Carts than Any Advertisements
ei.subject: 11월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Shills Worked Better for Using Carts than Any Advertisements

fullPassage: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily accomplished what logic, explanations, and advertisements failed to do. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.

questions.passage: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not (A)[discourage / persuade] his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were (B)[eager / reluctant] because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily (C)[accomplished / failed] what logic, explanations, and advertisements failed to do. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) persuade=설득하다, (B) reluctant=꺼리는, (C) accomplished=달성했다
det.analysis:
❌ ① discourage — reluctant — accomplished: (A) discourage(단념시키다)는 persuade(설득하다)의 반의어
❌ ② persuade — eager — accomplished: (B) eager(열망하는)는 reluctant(꺼리는)의 반의어
✅ ③ persuade — reluctant — accomplished: 원문 일치. 설득(persuade)하지 못함, 남성들이 꺼림(reluctant), 가짜 고객이 달성(accomplished) ←정답
❌ ④ persuade — reluctant — failed: (C) failed(실패했다)는 accomplished(달성했다)의 반의어

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) excellent=훌륭한, (B) attractive=매력적인, (C) readily=기꺼이
det.analysis:
❌ ① excellent — attractive — reluctantly: (C) reluctantly(마지못해)는 readily(기꺼이)의 반의어
❌ ② useless — attractive — readily: (A) useless(쓸모없는)는 excellent(훌륭한)의 반의어
❌ ③ excellent — repulsive — readily: (B) repulsive(혐오스러운)는 attractive(매력적인)의 반의어

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) repeated=반복된, (B) disguised=변장한, (C) accepted=수용했다
det.analysis:
❌ ① repeated — disguised — rejected: (C) rejected(거부했다)는 accepted(수용했다)의 반의어
❌ ② occasional — disguised — accepted: (A) occasional(가끔의)은 repeated(반복된)의 반의어
❌ ③ repeated — recognized — accepted: (B) recognized(알아본)은 disguised(변장한)의 반의어

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 남성들이 카트 사용을 꺼렸다는 맥락. willing(기꺼이 하는)은 reluctant(꺼리는)의 반의어
det.analysis:

det.korean: 몇 주 만에 고객들이 기꺼이 카트를 받아들였다는 맥락. reluctantly(마지못해)는 readily(기꺼이)의 반의어
det.analysis:
❌ ① excellent — 원문 일치. '훌륭한' 장치라는 맥락에 적절

det.korean: 남성들이 카트를 밀면 약해 보일 것이라 생각했다는 맥락. strong(강한)은 weak(약한)의 반의어

questions.passage: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was __________. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily accomplished what logic, explanations, and advertisements failed to do. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.

❌ ④ the final warning: 최후 경고는 본문에 없음
